definition: Carryover is an accounting method by which the deductions and credits of a taxable year that are either not used in that year, or could not be considered entirely in that year, are then applied to reduce the tax liability of later/subsequent years. Some of the items which may be carried over might include net operating losses, charitable contributions, and investment tax credits, etc. carrier / carryover Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026 There is another concept called a carryover basis, which is used to transfer a previous owner's original investment amount (plus improvements) to a subsequent owner for the purpose of calculating gain or loss upon a sale or exchange of an asset. Carryover is also used in other contexts, such as carryover of accrued vacation time or credits earned toward satisfying a minimum requirement in a degree course, etc. (See also: carryback)
